parole.testo: From Greek σκουμπρί (skoumprí), from Ancient Greek σκομβρίς (skombrís), from σκόμβρος (skómbros).

Apparently from Greek χαβιάρι (chaviári), from Byzantine Greek χαβιάρι (khabiári), from Ottoman Turkish خاویار (havyar), from Persian خاویار (xâvyâr). Doublet of كَافْيَار (kafyār) from French or English.

Likely from Greek γαρίδες (garídes, “shrimps”), from Ancient Greek κᾱρῖδες (kārîdes, “shrimps”), possibly influenced by the Arabic root ق ر د س (q r d s) or taken as the diminutive of قُرْدُوس (qurdūs), a rare derivation of قُرْد (qurd, “tick”).
